title: Region-aware routing matrix and capacity-first failover
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Our existing routing behavior favors latency-only steering and does not account for upstream capacity constraints or per-customer geo pinning. This leads to SLO violations during regional capacity pressure and accidental cross-region routing for customers with data residency needs. Goal: Define and implement a region-aware routing policy matrix that composes latency-based routing, geo pinning, and capacity-aware steering with deterministic precedence rules and configurable per-customer overrides.
proposal: Introduce a routing policy matrix evaluated in priority order: 1) Geo Pinning/Legal Constraints (hard constraint), 2) Capacity-aware steering (soft constraint with capacity budgets), 3) Latency-based routing (SLA/SL0 optimization), 4) Cost-tier fallback. Each request evaluated against: request attributes (customer id, requested region, pinned region flag), real-time capacity signals (available GPU slots, queue length), and latency heatmap (p90/p99). Implement a lightweight policy engine in the control plane that returns: target region, model variant, and a list of fallback regions. Add capability for per-customer overrides (pinning strictness: strict|prefer|none) and global circuit-breaker hooks that open on capacity SLO breaches.
decision: Approved design to use precedence matrix with geo pinning as a hard constraint and capacity-aware steering as the first soft constraint. We will not rely solely on instantaneous queue length; instead use short-window rate-limited capacity signals (1m decayed moving average) and open a regional circuit breaker when usable capacity < 15% for 2 consecutive minutes. Latency routing remains the tie-breaker. This balances user latency with availability and tenancy guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy engine returns deterministic target region for >99.9% of requests within 2ms decision latency
During synthetic regional congestion tests, per-customer pinned-strong requests never leave pinned region (unless operator override)
When a regional circuit breaker trips, traffic is steered to capacity-favored regions and global error budget burn does not exceed 5% over baseline
End-to-end P90 generation latency for routed requests meets existing SLOs 95% of the time in normal traffic
Automated canary rollout with metrics-based approval and rollback integrated into console rollouts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Feature flag behind 'regional-matrix-v1' for internal traffic only
Phase 2 - Canary with 5% of production traffic (non-enterprise customers), monitor key metrics for 24h
Phase 3 - Enable per-customer 'prefer' pinning for customers with residency requirements, sample logs to ensure compliance
Phase 4 - Gradual ramp to 50% traffic with capacity-aware steering enabled, continue telemetry checks
Phase 5 - Enterprise opt-in and global flip after 2 weeks of stable canary and signoff from SRE and Security
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence and per-customer override parsing
E2E integration test using local routing simulator with injected capacity signals
Load test that simulates regional GPU exhaustion and verifies failover and circuit breaker behavior (Datadog and k6 harness)
Chaos test: regional network partition while ensuring pinned traffic remains pinned or flagged for operator intervention
Regression test: ensure latency-based routing still selected when capacity is unconstrained
monitoring_and_slo: SLOs: P99 decision latency < 10ms for policy engine, P90 generation latency SLO unchanged (as existing runtime SLO)
SLO indicators: region_capacity_utilization, region_available_slots, policy_decision_latency, routing_failure_rate, cross_region_violations
Dashboards: new 'Regional Routing Matrix' dashboard in Datadog with per-region capacity, pin-violation alerts, and circuit-breaker state
Alerts: page when regional usable_capacity < 10% OR routing_failure_rate > 0.5% for 5m
circuit_breaker_config: Half-open probe: route 1% of traffic every 30s to check capacity recovery
Backoff policy: exponential backoff with base 30s, max 15m
Operator controls: manual open/close and override with annotated audit log entries
Circuit-breaker state exposed via /v1/internal/routing/state for observability
load_shedding_policy: Graceful degradation order: 1) non-critical retries & deferred batches, 2) lower-cost quantized model variant, 3) reduce max_tokens per request, 4) shed best-effort low-priority traffic based on tenant priority buckets
Per-tenant guarantees: reserve minimal capacity slices for enterprise customers with contracts, configurable via tenant profile
Shedding signals derived from combined metric: (region_queue_length_weighted + cpu_backpressure + gpu_utilization) / capacity_budget
Shedding action logged with reason codes and per-request headers indicating applied policy

notes: Trade-off: Using a decayed moving average for capacity reduces flapping but increases reaction time to sudden failures - acceptable because our circuit breaker probes reduce blind time
